title: Bosnia Holds Elections as Leader Declares Victory for His Party
summary:
Voters in Bosnia and Herzegovina went to the polls on Sunday in an election shaped by money worries, the country's hopes of joining the European Union, and long-standing divisions between ethnic groups. Those divisions date back to a war in the early 1990s.

Milorad Dodik, a Bosnian Serb nationalist politician, declared victory for his party. Dodik was not on the ballot. He was banned from public office after being convicted last year of defying decisions by the international official who oversees the 1995 peace agreement that ended the war. Even so, he has been central to the campaign. He supports Russia and has called for parts of the country to separate, which has made some people fear new instability.

With nearly 90 percent of votes counted, Dodik's ally Zeljka Cvijanovic had more than 55 percent for the Serb seat on Bosnia's three-member presidency. She led her nearest opponent by about 30 points. At a news conference, Dodik gave credit to U.S. President Donald Trump's 2024 election win and to Russian President Vladimir Putin's support. "No one should ask us to change our politics," he said.

Other candidates also claimed victory before counting was finished. They included Darijana Filipovic for the Croat seat and Denis Becirovic for the Bosniak seat, who held a lead of fewer than three percentage points. Around 3.4 million people were eligible to vote.

Bosnia's government was built by a U.S.-brokered peace deal to balance the Bosniak, Serb and Croat communities. Many people vote along ethnic lines, which has slowed progress toward joining the EU. This was the first Bosnian election to use electronic voter identification and ballot scanners to help prevent cheating. These are not final results.
why_it_matters: The election shows how Bosnia's political system, built to balance different communities, still faces ethnic divisions that slow its progress toward joining the EU.

questions.question: What shaped Bosnia's Sunday election?
options: A big storm that closed roads
A new national flag and anthem
A change in the school year for all students
Money worries, hopes of joining the EU, and ethnic divisions
questions.correct_answer: Money worries, hopes of joining the EU, and ethnic divisions

questions.question: Why was Dodik banned from public office?
options: He lost an earlier election badly
He asked to leave office himself
He was convicted last year of defying an international official's decisions
He was too old to run for any office
questions.correct_answer: He was convicted last year of defying an international official's decisions

questions.question: How many members does Bosnia's presidency have?
options: One
Twelve
Three
Five

questions.question: Who did Dodik give credit to for his party's win?
options: Trump's 2024 election win and Putin's support
The Bosnian army and the police
The courts in the capital Sarajevo
The European Union and the United Nations
questions.correct_answer: Trump's 2024 election win and Putin's support

questions.question: Which new technology was used in this election for the first time?
options: Voting by phone app from home
Voting from space stations
Electronic voter identification and ballot scanners
Robot poll workers at every site
questions.correct_answer: Electronic voter identification and ballot scanners

questions.question: What made some people fear new instability?
options: A teachers' strike across the country
A flood in the capital city
A new tax on all goods
Dodik's pro-Russia stance and calls for parts of the country to separate
questions.correct_answer: Dodik's pro-Russia stance and calls for parts of the country to separate
